definition_zh: 收购；获得；习得；购得物
definition_en: the act of gaining something, especially the buying of a company or the learning of a skill
core_image: 一份合同签完，另一家公司的招牌被换下来
scene: 收购那家对手公司，前后花了好几个月。 The acquisition of the rival firm took months.
sceneCN: 这里的 acquisition 是「收购」（第 1 个义项：买下企业）；句意是收购对手公司花了几个月。

derivatives.zh: 由名词去后缀还原为动词，义为「获得；收购」
由动词加表示施动者的后缀构成，义为「收购方」
由词干加形容词后缀构成，义为「贪得的」
由过去分词转化而来，义为「后天获得的」

senses.title: The buying of a company
senses.definition: the purchase of one business by another
senses.definitionCN: 一家企业买下另一家企业
senses.example: The acquisition added three factories to the group.
senses.exampleCN: 这次收购为集团增加了三家工厂。
senses.why: The noun turns the act of gaining into a business event, and in finance the most visible gain is a bought rival.
senses.whyCN: 名词把「取得」变成一个商业事件，而在金融里最显眼的取得，就是买下一家对手。

senses.title: The gaining of knowledge or skill
senses.definition: the process of coming to have information or an ability
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐拥有知识或能力的过程
senses.example: The acquisition of a new language takes years.
senses.exampleCN: 掌握一门新语言需要多年。
senses.why: What is bought in business is learned in the mind, so the same noun names the slow gaining of a skill.
senses.whyCN: 商业里用钱买的东西，在头脑里靠学得来，于是同一个名词也指技能缓慢到手的过程。

senses.title: Something newly obtained
senses.definition: an object that has recently been gained, especially by a museum
senses.definitionCN: 最近得到的东西，尤指博物馆的新藏品
senses.example: The painting is the museum's latest acquisition.
senses.exampleCN: 这幅画是博物馆最新入藏的藏品。
senses.why: From the act comes the object: once the deal closes, the thing bought stands in the room and is called an acquisition.
senses.whyCN: 从行为落到物件：交易一完成，买来的东西就摆在屋里，被称作一件 acquisition。

intro.en: The noun is the Latin action noun of the verb for seeking and gaining.
intro.cn: 这个名词是拉丁语中「寻求并获得」动词的动作名词。

items.en: quaerere meant to seek.
items.cn: quaerere 意为寻找。

items.en: acquirere meant to gain by seeking.
items.cn: acquirere 意为寻求而得到。

items.en: acquisitio named the act of gaining.
items.cn: acquisitio 指取得的行为。

items.en: acquisition entered English as a noun of obtaining.
items.cn: acquisition 在十五世纪进入英语，是表示获得的名词。

items.en: finance gave it the dominant sense of buying a company.
items.cn: 金融赋予了它「买下公司」这一主要含义。

note.en: The first group is the acquire family; the second is other words for a purchase or gain.
note.cn: 第一组是 acquire 词族；第二组是别的表示购买或获得的词。

abstract.cn: 想象旧招牌被拧下来，新招牌被吊上去。

examples.en: Reading widely speeds the acquisition of vocabulary.

examples.en: The sculpture is the gallery's most valuable acquisition.

definition_zh: 股东；持有公司股份的人或机构
definition_en: a person or organization that owns shares in a company
core_image: 公司被切成许多等份，一只手握住其中一份并举起表决卡
scene: 年度股东大会开始前，一位持有公司股份的人翻看表决材料，抬头询问董事会为何没有派发利润。 The shareholder asked the board why profits were not paid out.
sceneCN: 这里指「持有公司股份的人或机构」，对应第 1 个义项：公司股份的持有人；句意为这位股东问董事会为什么利润没有分派出去。画面要点：会议室长桌、表决材料、持股凭证。

pos.zh: 股东；股份持有人（可指个人、基金或其他机构）

collocations.zh: 多数股东；持股过半的股东
积极干预公司治理的股东

derivatives.zh: 多处持股；持有的股份总额

senses.title: Owner of part of a company
senses.titleCN: 持有公司一部分股份的人
senses.definition: a person who owns one or more shares in a company
senses.definitionCN: 持有一家公司一份或多份股份的人
senses.example: Every shareholder receives a copy of the annual report.
senses.exampleCN: 每位股东都会收到一份年度报告。
senses.why: Share names a divided portion of something and holder names the one who keeps it, so the word literally means the keeper of a portion of the company.
senses.whyCN: share 指从整体中分出的一份，holder 指持有者，所以这个词字面上就是「公司某一份的持有者」。

senses.title: Holder of a controlling stake
senses.titleCN: 持股足以控制公司的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder whose stake is large enough to direct the company
senses.definitionCN: 持股比例大到足以左右公司决策的股东
senses.example: The controlling shareholder can appoint most of the board.
senses.exampleCN: 控股股东能够任命董事会的大部分成员。
senses.why: The same ownership relation is read by weight: when the held portion passes a threshold, the keeper of that portion gains the power to steer the whole.
senses.whyCN: 同样的持有关系按分量来读：当握有的那一份越过某个门槛，这一份的持有者就获得了左右整体的权力。

senses.title: Holder of a small stake
senses.definition: a shareholder whose stake is too small to influence control
senses.definitionCN: 持股比例较小、无法左右控制权的股东
senses.example: Minority shareholders joined forces to block the sale.
senses.exampleCN: 少数股东联合起来阻止这笔出售。
senses.why: Minority keeps the core meaning and adds scale: the portion is real but its weight is light, so the owner has a claim without command.
senses.whyCN: minority 保留核心义而补充了分量：那一份确实存在，但分量很轻，于是持有者有收益主张却没有指挥权。

senses.title: Institution as owner
senses.titleCN: 以机构身份持股的股东
senses.definition: a fund, pension scheme, insurer or other organization that holds shares
senses.definitionCN: 基金、养老金、保险公司等持有股份的组织
senses.example: Institutional shareholders pressed for clearer climate disclosures.
senses.exampleCN: 机构股东要求更清晰的气候信息披露。
senses.why: The holder here is not a single person but an organization acting as one legal owner, so the core sense is applied to a collective body.
senses.whyCN: 这里的持有者不是单个自然人，而是作为一个法律主体行事的组织，核心义因此落在一个集体身上。

senses.title: Private individual as owner
senses.titleCN: 以个人身份持股的股东
senses.definition: an ordinary private investor who owns shares directly
senses.definitionCN: 直接持有股份的普通个人投资者
senses.example: Retail shareholders often hold only a few dozen shares.
senses.exampleCN: 个人股东往往只持有几十股。
senses.why: Retail marks the opposite of institutional: the same legal relation is held in a private hand and on a small scale.
senses.whyCN: retail 标出与机构相反的一面：同样的法律关系握在私人手里，规模也小。

senses.title: Owner as a claim on value
senses.definition: the owner whose financial interest a company is said to serve
senses.definitionCN: 公司被说成应当为其财务利益服务的持股方
senses.example: The takeover was justified as a way to maximize shareholder value.
senses.exampleCN: 这场收购被辩解为最大化股东价值的手段。
senses.why: Once ownership is abstracted from a person to a financial claim, the shareholder becomes a stand-in for the value that the portion represents.
senses.whyCN: 当所有权从具体的人抽象成一项财务主张，股东就成了那一份所代表价值的代称。

senses.title: Voter in corporate governance
senses.titleCN: 在公司治理中投票的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder exercising voting rights at a meeting
senses.definitionCN: 在股东会议上行使表决权的持股人
senses.example: Shareholders voted against the proposed pay package.
senses.exampleCN: 股东投票否决了拟议的薪酬方案。
senses.why: A share carries a vote as well as a dividend, so the keeper of a portion also becomes a participant in deciding how the company is run.
senses.whyCN: 股份除了带来股息，也带来表决权，因此这一份的持有者同时成为公司如何运转的决策参与者。

senses.title: Activist owner pressing for change
senses.titleCN: 积极推动公司改变的股东
senses.definition: a shareholder who publicly campaigns to change company policy or leadership
senses.definitionCN: 公开推动公司改变政策或领导层的股东
senses.example: An activist shareholder nominated three new directors.
senses.exampleCN: 一位积极股东提名了三位新董事。
senses.why: Here the voting and value senses combine: the owner uses the stake as leverage to force a change rather than merely to receive a return.
senses.whyCN: 这里投票义与价值义合并：持有者把股份当作杠杆去迫使改变，而不只是领取回报。

intro.en: Shareholder is an English compound of share and holder, built from Old English material rather than borrowed from Latin. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: shareholder 是 share 与 holder 构成的英语复合词，用的是古英语材料，而非借自拉丁语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Scearu meant a division, portion or allotted part, and it is generally thought to be related to scieran 'to cut, shear', so a share is literally a piece cut off from a whole.
items.cn: scearu 意为「划分、份额、分得的部分」，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词，因此「一份」本义就是从整体上切下来的一块。

items.en: Healdan meant to hold, keep or watch over, and its agent form holder named the one who keeps something in hand.
items.cn: healdan 意为「持有、保管、看守」，其表人形式 holder 指把某物握在手中的人。

items.en: By the Middle English period holder was a settled noun for a person who possesses land, an office or an object.
items.cn: 到中古英语时期，holder 已经是稳定的名词，指拥有土地、职位或物品的人。

items.en: Joint-stock companies divided their capital into transferable portions, and the compound shareholder named the person who kept one of those portions. The first recorded uses are dated to the early eighteenth century.
items.cn: 合股公司把资本分成可转让的份额，复合词 shareholder 便用来指持有其中一份的人。已知最早用例一般定在十八世纪早期。

items.en: Industrial finance widened the word to institutions and private savers alike, and later governance debates added the controlling, minority and activist readings.
items.cn: 工业化金融把这个词扩展到机构与个人储蓄者，后来的治理讨论又添上控股、少数与积极干预等读法。

note.en: The first group looks or sounds close to shareholder but differs in formation; the second group shares the idea of owning a stake without being the same word.
note.cn: 第一组在拼写或构成上与 shareholder 相近，但构词不同；第二组同样表示「持有份额」，却不是同一个词。

entries.definition: A near synonym built on stock rather than share; American English prefers it, but the two words describe the same legal position.
entries.definitionCN: 用 stock 而非 share 构成的近义说法；美式英语更常用它，但两个词描述的是同一种法律地位。

entries.definition: Originally the holder of a bet or a stake in a wager, now any party affected by a company; a stakeholder need not own a single share.
entries.definitionCN: 原指赌注的持有者，现指受公司影响的任何一方；利益相关者未必持有一股股份。

entries.definition: A rarer synonym formed with owner; it stresses ownership rather than the act of holding.
entries.definitionCN: 较少见的同义说法，用 owner 构成，强调所有权而不是「持有」这个动作。

entries.definition: A farmer who works land for a share of the crop; the share here is harvest, not capital, and the word has no connection with company ownership.
entries.definitionCN: 按收成份额耕种他人土地的人；这里的 share 指收成而非资本，与公司所有权无关。

entries.definition: Anyone who puts money into an asset hoping for a return; an investor may hold bonds or property and need not own shares.
entries.definitionCN: 把资金投入资产以求得回报的人；投资者可能持有债券或房产，未必持有股份。

entries.definition: A descriptive phrase for a holder of equity, used when the legal nature of the ownership matters more than the person.
entries.definitionCN: 对权益持有者的描述性说法，用于强调所有权的法律性质而非持有人本身。

entries.definition: In company law, especially British usage, a member is a person entered on the register of members, which in practice means a shareholder.
entries.definitionCN: 在公司法、尤其是英式用法中，member 指登记在公司成员名册上的人，实务上就是股东。

entries.definition: A party who acts for itself in a transaction, as opposed to an agent; the word marks a role in the deal, not ownership of shares.
entries.definitionCN: 在交易中代表自己行事的一方，与代理人相对；它标出交易角色，而不表示持有股份。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Share plus holder: the person who holds one of the cut portions of a company.
normal.cn: share 加 holder：持有公司被切出的其中一份的人。

normal.en: The Old English noun behind share meant a division or allotted part, so ownership is pictured as holding a cut slice.
normal.cn: share 背后的古英语名词本义是划分或分得的部分，所以所有权可以想成握着一片切下来的份。

normal.en: Stockholder is the American twin; both point to the same register of owners.
normal.cn: stockholder 是美式英语里的对应词；两者指向同一份所有者名册。

normal.en: Fixed phrases sort the word by size and by owner type: majority, minority, controlling, institutional, activist.
normal.cn: 固定搭配按规模与持有人类型给这个词分类：多数、少数、控股、机构、积极干预。

normal.en: A shareholder owns shares; a stakeholder merely has something at stake, which is the distinction to keep in mind.
normal.cn: shareholder 拥有股份；stakeholder 只是有利益牵涉，这个区别要记牢。

abstract.en: Picture a company as a pie cut into equal slices, with one slice wrapped in a document and kept in a pocket.
abstract.cn: 把公司想成一块切成等份的饼，其中一份用文件包好，收在口袋里。

abstract.en: Picture a voting card whose weight is set by how many slices the hand already holds.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表决卡，它的分量由那只手已经握住的份数决定。

abstract.en: Picture a claim on a stream of future profit, drawn as a thin line running from the company to a waiting hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一项对未来利润的权利，画成一条从公司流向等待之手的细线。

examples.en: The largest shareholder blocked the merger at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 最大股东在年度会议上阻止了这次合并。

examples.en: Shareholders expect the dividend to rise with profits.
examples.cn: 股东期待股息随利润一同提高。

examples.en: A pension fund can be a patient shareholder for many years.
examples.cn: 养老基金可以多年做一位有耐心的股东。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「share（一份）+ holder（持有者）」——持有公司一份的人 → 股东

root: share 出自古英语 scearu「划分、份额」，一般认为是 scieran「切、剪」的同族词；holder 由 hold「持有」加表人后缀构成。整个词是英语本族复合词，不来自拉丁语。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses unfold from one relation: a person keeps a divided portion of a company, and that portion is then read by weight, by owner type, by value, by vote and by pressure.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项由同一种关系展开：一个人持有公司被分出的一份，这一份再按分量、持有人类型、价值、表决与施压等角度被读出。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a company cut into equal slices, one slice held in a hand together with a voting card.
core.cn: 核心意象：公司被切成等份，一只手握着其中一份，同时拿着表决卡。

branches.en: BASE RELATION: the word itself is simply the keeper of one cut portion of the company.
branches.cn: 基础关系：这个词本身就是公司某一份的持有者。

branches.en: WEIGHT OF THE SLICE: a large portion can steer the whole, while a small portion can only object.
branches.cn: 那一份的分量：大份能左右整体，小份只能表示反对。

branches.en: WHO HOLDS IT: the same portion can rest in an organization or in a private hand.
branches.cn: 由谁持有：同一份既可以归机构，也可以归个人。

branches.en: VALUE CLAIM: ownership abstracted into the financial interest that the company is told to serve.
branches.cn: 价值主张：所有权被抽象为公司被要求去服务的财务利益。

branches.en: VOICE AND PRESSURE: the voting card turns the held portion into a say in how the company is run.
branches.cn: 表决与施压：表决卡把握有的那一份变成对公司运转的发言权。

intro.en: Shareholder is made of native English pieces, so its family is built by compounding and by the agent suffix rather than by Latin derivation.
intro.cn: shareholder 由英语本族成分构成，因此它的词族靠复合与表人后缀扩展，而不是靠拉丁语派生。

latinIntro.en: No Latin word lies behind this compound. Latin-based finance vocabulary enters English separately through words such as equity, capital and dividend.
latinIntro.cn: 这个复合词背后没有拉丁词。拉丁来源的金融词汇是通过 equity、capital、dividend 等词另行进入英语的。

items.structure: share (Old English noun, a division or portion)

items.example: Each child took a share of the fruit.
items.exampleCN: 每个孩子都分到了一份水果。

items.structure: hold (Old English verb, to keep or watch over)
items.example: She held the deed in her hand.
items.exampleCN: 她把契据握在手里。

items.structure: -er (Old English agent suffix, one who does or keeps)
items.example: The keeper of the key opened the door.
items.exampleCN: 拿钥匙的人打开了门。

items.meaning: the keeper of a portion of a company
items.example: A shareholder may vote at the meeting.

definition_zh: 股息；红利；被除数；回报
definition_en: a share of profit paid to shareholders, or a number to be divided
core_image: 一只钱袋被分成几小袋，递给持有股份的人
scene: 公司年报公布后，董事会决定把更多利润以现金分给持股人。 The board raised the dividend after a strong year.
sceneCN: 这里指「分给股东的利润」，对应第 1 个义项：公司从利润中按股份支付给股东的款项；句意为业绩强劲的一年后，董事会提高了股息。画面要点：年报、钱袋、股东名单。

pos.zh: 股息；红利；被除数；回报；保单红利

senses.title: A share of profit paid to shareholders
senses.definition: a part of a company's profit distributed to its shareholders
senses.definitionCN: 公司利润中分给股东的一部分
senses.example: The company pays a dividend twice a year.
senses.exampleCN: 这家公司每年派发两次股息。
senses.why: The word literally means that which is to be divided: profit is cut into portions and one portion goes to each share.
senses.whyCN: 这个词字面上指「应当被分掉的东西」：利润被切成几份，每份股份得一份。

senses.title: An interim or final payment
senses.titleCN: 期中或期末派发的股息
senses.definition: a dividend paid at a scheduled point in the financial year
senses.definitionCN: 在财年某个既定节点支付的股息
senses.example: The interim dividend rose to eight cents.
senses.exampleCN: 期中股息升至八分。
senses.why: The same share of profit is named by its timing, since a payment can be made halfway through the year or at its close.
senses.whyCN: 同一份利润按支付时点得名，因为款项可以在年中或年末支付。

senses.title: A benefit from an action
senses.definition: an advantage or return that results from effort or investment
senses.definitionCN: 由努力或投入产生的益处或回报
senses.example: The training paid dividends in fewer accidents.
senses.exampleCN: 这项培训在减少事故上带来了回报。
senses.why: Profit is abstracted from money to any good result, so an effort can be said to pay dividends even without shares.
senses.whyCN: 利润从金钱抽象为任何好结果，所以即使没有股份，一项努力也能说带来回报。

senses.title: A number to be divided
senses.definition: the number that is divided by another in arithmetic
senses.definitionCN: 算术中被另一个数除的数
senses.example: In twelve divided by three, twelve is the dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 在十二除以三中，十二是被除数。
senses.why: This is the oldest literal sense: the quantity that is cut up by division, before finance borrowed the name.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的字面义：被除法切分的数量，金融后来借用了这个名字。

senses.title: An insurance policy dividend
senses.definition: a share of surplus returned to holders of certain insurance policies
senses.definitionCN: 某些保险保单持有人分得的盈余份额
senses.example: The mutual insurer returned a dividend to policyholders.
senses.exampleCN: 这家互助保险公司向保单持有人返还了红利。
senses.why: An insurer's surplus is divided among the people who funded it, so the profit-share sense moves from shares to policies.
senses.whyCN: 保险公司的盈余在出资人之间分配，利润份额义于是从股份转到保单。

senses.title: A cooperative patronage dividend
senses.titleCN: 合作社按交易量分配的盈余
senses.definition: a share of a cooperative's surplus returned according to members' trade
senses.definitionCN: 合作社按成员交易额返还的盈余份额
senses.example: The farmers' cooperative paid a patronage dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 农民合作社支付了按交易额计算的盈余。
senses.why: Cooperative members are owners and customers at once, so surplus is divided by how much each used the business.
senses.whyCN: 合作社成员同时是所有者与顾客，所以盈余按各人使用企业的多少来分。

senses.title: A dividend paid in shares
senses.definition: a distribution made by issuing additional shares instead of cash
senses.definitionCN: 通过增发股份而非现金进行的分配
senses.example: The company chose a stock dividend to keep cash.
senses.exampleCN: 公司选择股票股利以保留现金。
senses.why: The portion is still divided out, but the portion consists of new shares rather than money.
senses.whyCN: 分出去的仍然是份额，只是这一份由新股份而不是现金构成。

senses.title: A dividend paid in cash
senses.definition: a distribution paid directly in money
senses.definitionCN: 直接以金钱支付的分配
senses.example: Investors prefer a steady cash dividend.
senses.exampleCN: 投资者偏好稳定的现金股息。
senses.why: This is the plainest financial reading: profit is divided and the holder receives money rather than paper.
senses.whyCN: 这是最朴素的金融读法：利润被分开，持有人收到的是钱而不是纸。

intro.en: Dividend comes from a Latin gerundive meaning that which is to be divided; the arithmetic sense is older than the financial one. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: dividend 出自拉丁语动形词，意为「应当被分掉的东西」；算术义早于金融义。年代均为约数。

items.en: Dividere meant to force apart, cleave or distribute; it is generally analysed as dis- 'apart' plus a second element meaning to separate, though the deeper origin of that element is source uncertain.
items.cn: dividere 意为分开、劈开、分配；一般分析为 dis-「分开」加一个表示「分离」的成分，但该成分更深的来源不确定。

items.en: The gerundive dividendum meant that which is to be divided, a form used in arithmetic and in sharing out amounts.
items.cn: 动形词 dividendum 意为「应当被分掉的东西」，用于算术与分配数额。

items.en: English arithmetic books used dividend for the number to be divided, the sense that still survives in mathematics.
items.cn: 十六世纪英语算术书用 dividend 指被除数，这一义项至今留在数学中。

items.en: Joint-stock companies began to divide surplus profit among shareholders and called each portion a dividend.
items.cn: 合股公司开始把剩余利润分给股东，并把每一份称为 dividend。

items.en: Insurance, cooperatives and stock-based payments extended the word to policyholders, members and shares issued instead of cash.
items.cn: 保险、合作社与以股代现的支付方式，把这个词扩展到保单持有人、合作社成员与增发股份。

note.en: The first group is built on the same dividing root and is easily confused; the second group names other kinds of payment or return.
note.cn: 第一组建立在同一个「分开」的词根上，容易混淆；第二组是其他类型的支付或回报。

entries.definition: The number by which another is divided; the dividend is above the line, the divisor below it.
entries.definitionCN: 用来除另一个数的数；被除数在除号上方，除数在下方。

entries.definition: The act or operation of dividing; it is the process, while a dividend is one of the quantities involved.
entries.definitionCN: 划分或除的动作；它是过程，而 dividend 是参与其中的一个量。

entries.definition: To separate or share out; the verb names the action that produces a dividend.
entries.definitionCN: 分开或分配；动词表示产生股息或被除数的动作。

entries.definition: A single person, literally one that cannot be divided; it shares the root but has no sense of a portion paid out.
entries.definitionCN: 单个的人，字面是「不可再分者」；共享词根，但没有分出份额的意思。

entries.definition: A sum of money paid out, from insurance, gambling or a company; it is broader than dividend.
entries.definitionCN: 从保险、博彩或公司付出的款项；比股息更宽泛。

entries.definition: The formal sharing out of money or assets; a dividend is one kind of distribution.
entries.definitionCN: 对金钱或资产的正式分配；股息是分配的一种。

entries.definition: An extra payment, often discretionary; a dividend follows ownership, while a bonus often follows performance.
entries.definitionCN: 额外支付的款项，常出于酌情；股息跟随所有权，奖金常跟随业绩。

entries.definition: The total gain from an investment, including interest and price change; a dividend is only one part of a return.
entries.definitionCN: 投资的总收益，包括利息与价格变化；股息只是回报的一部分。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real Latin meaning that which is to be divided, real fixed phrases and real arithmetic relatives.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的拉丁语「应当被分掉者」、真实固定搭配与真实算术同族词。

normal.en: The word is the thing to be divided, which explains both the arithmetic and the financial senses.
normal.cn: 这个词就是「要被分掉的东西」，这同时解释了算术义与金融义。

normal.en: Profit is cut into portions, and each share receives one portion.
normal.cn: 利润被切成几份，每一股得到其中一份。

normal.en: Insurance surplus and cooperative surplus are divided the same way among the people who funded them.
normal.cn: 保险盈余与合作社盈余也按同样方式在出资人之间分配。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the finance sense: dividend yield, cash dividend, stock dividend.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出金融义：股息收益率、现金股息、股票股利。

normal.en: The phrase pay dividends keeps the metaphor alive: effort is an investment that can return a portion.
normal.cn: 「产生回报」这一说法保留了比喻：努力是一项能返回一份的投资。

abstract.en: Picture a money bag opened and its contents split into small bags for the people who own the company.
abstract.cn: 想象一只钱袋被打开，里面的钱分成小袋，交给拥有公司的人。

abstract.en: Picture the same splitting action drawn as a number above a line, waiting to be divided.
abstract.cn: 想象同一个分配动作画成横线上方的一个数，等待被除。

abstract.en: Picture a seed of effort later opening into several small bags of benefit.
abstract.cn: 想象一粒努力的种子后来裂开成几小袋好处。

examples.en: Shareholders approved the higher dividend at the annual meeting.
examples.cn: 股东们在年度会议上批准了更高的股息。

examples.en: Patience with the new process paid dividends within a year.
examples.cn: 对新流程的耐心在一年内带来了回报。

examples.en: In the expression forty divided by eight, forty is the dividend.
examples.cn: 在四十除以八这个算式中，四十是被除数。

root: 拉丁语 dividere「分开、分配」的动形词 dividendum「应当被分掉的东西」；先用于算术的被除数，十七世纪起用于分给股东的利润份额。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses all depend on division: a profit is cut into portions, a scheduled payment is named by its timing, the benefit spreads beyond money, and arithmetic keeps the oldest literal sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都依赖「分开」：利润被切成几份，按支付时点得名，好处超出金钱，而算术保留了最古老的字面义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a money bag split into small bags for the people who own the company.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只钱袋被分成小袋，交给拥有公司的人。

branches.en: CORE SHARE: profit is divided, and one portion follows each share.
branches.cn: 核心份额：利润被分开，每一股跟随一份。

branches.en: FORMS OF PAYMENT: the same portion can be interim or final, paid in cash or issued as shares.
branches.cn: 支付形式：同一份可以是期中或期末，以现金支付或以股份发放。

branches.en: BENEFIT: the divided portion becomes any good result that effort returns.
branches.cn: 好处：被分出的份额变成努力返回的任何好结果。

branches.en: ARITHMETIC: the quantity that is to be divided keeps the oldest literal meaning.
branches.cn: 算术：应当被除的那个量保留了最古老的字面义。

branches.en: OTHER SURPLUS: insurers and cooperatives divide surplus among policyholders and members.
branches.cn: 其他盈余：保险公司与合作社在保单持有人与成员之间分配盈余。

intro.en: Dividend belongs to the Latin family of dividere, whose pieces still appear in English words about separation and arithmetic.
intro.cn: dividend 属于拉丁语 dividere 一族，其成分仍出现在表示分离与算术的英语词中。

latinIntro.en: Latin dividere 'to divide' gives divide, division, divisor and individual, literally one who cannot be divided.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 dividere「分开」衍生 divide、division、divisor 与 individual，后者字面是「不可再分者」。

definition_zh: 公平；公正；股权；权益；资产净值；衡平法
definition_en: fairness in the way people are treated, or the value of an owner's share in an asset
core_image: 水灾过后，富户能搬进旅馆，穷人只能住体育馆，市议会按实际损失发放补助，努力把起点上的差距补平
scene: 洪水过后议事会分发救济。 The council distributed relief with an eye to equity rather than equal shares.
sceneCN: 此处指「按实际需要与损失分配、以求结果公平」（第 1 个义项：公正对待，而非机械平均）；句意为水灾之后，议会发放救济时看重的是公平，而非每人一份的平均分配。可辨识物件：临时旅馆、体育馆床位、补助登记表、泥水痕迹。

senses.title: Fairness in treatment
senses.definition: the quality of treating people justly, especially by adjusting for differences in need or disadvantage
senses.definitionCN: 公正待人的品质，尤指按需要或不利处境作出调整
senses.example: After the flood, the council distributed relief with an eye to equity rather than equal shares.
senses.exampleCN: 水灾之后，议会发放救济时看重的是公平，而非每人一份的平均分配。
senses.why: Equity comes from Latin aequitas 'evenness, fairness', from aequus 'level, even', so the base sense is a level scale rather than an identical portion.
senses.whyCN: equity 来自拉丁 aequitas「均平、公正」，词根 aequus「平的、相等的」，因此基础义是「把秤放平」，而非「每份一样」。

senses.title: An ownership stake
senses.definition: a share of ownership in a company or asset, giving a claim on its value
senses.definitionCN: 在公司或资产中的一份所有权，可对其价值提出主张
senses.example: The founders kept a small equity stake after the second round of funding.
senses.exampleCN: 第二轮融资后，创始人仍保留一小部分股权。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the word because a fair share of value is literally a share in the asset, so 'fairness' became 'ownership portion'.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用这个词，因为价值中「应得的一份」字面上就是资产中的一份，于是「公平」转为「所有权份额」。

senses.title: Net value of an asset
senses.definition: the value of an asset after all claims against it are subtracted, as in home equity
senses.definitionCN: 扣除全部相关债务后资产的剩余价值，如房屋净值
senses.example: Their equity in the house grew as the mortgage was paid down.
senses.exampleCN: 随着房贷逐步偿还，他们在这栋房子上的净值增加了。
senses.why: The accounting sense measures what is truly the owner's, which is the ownership sense reduced to a number.
senses.whyCN: 会计义衡量真正属于所有者的部分，也就是把所有权义化成一个数字。

senses.title: The law of equity
senses.definition: the body of English law developed to soften the strictness of common law and to provide fair remedies
senses.definitionCN: 为缓和普通法的严苛并提供公平救济而形成的英国法律体系
senses.example: The court of equity granted an injunction where the common law could only award damages.
senses.exampleCN: 衡平法院签发了禁令，而普通法只能判决损害赔偿。
senses.why: Legal history used the word for fairness itself, and the name stuck to the court that administered it.
senses.whyCN: 法律史直接用「公平」一词来称呼这套制度，名称便固定在执行它的法院上。

senses.title: Equal treatment policy
senses.definition: a policy that aims to remove barriers so that groups can reach the same opportunities
senses.definitionCN: 旨在消除障碍、使不同群体获得相同机会的政策
senses.example: The university adopted an equity plan for students from the hill villages.
senses.exampleCN: 这所大学为来自山村的学生制定了公平计划。
senses.why: Modern policy uses equity for the active removal of barriers, as distinct from formal equality of rules.
senses.whyCN: 现代政策用 equity 指主动消除障碍，与规则上的形式平等相区别。

senses.title: Residual claim in finance
senses.definition: the right of shareholders to what remains after all debts and other claims are paid
senses.definitionCN: 在清偿全部债务与其他主张后，股东对剩余部分的权利
senses.example: Equity holders are paid last, so they carry the greatest risk.
senses.exampleCN: 权益持有人最后受偿，因此承担最大风险。
senses.why: Because owners are paid last, the finance sense also names the riskiest claim, not just the largest one.
senses.whyCN: 由于所有者最后受偿，金融义也指风险最大的主张，而不只是最大的一份。

senses.title: Justice in distribution
senses.definition: the fairness of how goods, burdens and opportunities are distributed across a society
senses.definitionCN: 商品、负担与机会在一个社会中如何分配的公平性
senses.example: The report asked whether the tax system produced equity across the income scale.
senses.exampleCN: 报告追问税制是否在收入阶梯上实现了公平。
senses.why: Political philosophy widened the word from individual fairness to the fairness of a whole distribution.
senses.whyCN: 政治哲学把这个词从个人公平扩展到整个分配的公平。

senses.title: Equitable access in education
senses.definition: the principle that a person's background should not decide their access to schooling or support
senses.definitionCN: 一个人的出身不应决定其受教育或获得支持的机会这一原则
senses.example: Equity in admissions meant offering tutoring before the entrance test, not lowering the standard.
senses.exampleCN: 录取公平意味着在入学考试前提供辅导，而不是降低标准。
senses.why: Schools use the term for support given earlier, because fairness in access is judged by outcomes, not by identical treatment.
senses.whyCN: 学校用这个词指提前给予的支持，因为入学公平由结果衡量，而非由相同对待衡量。

intro.en: Equity comes from Latin aequitas 'evenness, fairness', from aequus 'level, even', through Old French. Its legal and financial senses grew in English. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: equity 经古法语来自拉丁 aequitas「均平、公正」，词根 aequus「平的、相等的」。其法律与金融义在英语中发展出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Aequus meant 'level, even, equal'. Its deeper origin is not established, and earlier forms proposed for it are reconstructions.
items.cn: aequus 意为「平的、均等的、相等的」。其更深来源未得到证明，凡为其提出的更早形态均属重构。

items.en: Aequitas named evenness and fairness, the quality of a level scale. It was also personified as a Roman virtue.
items.cn: aequitas 指均平与公正，即秤杆放平的性质，也曾被拟人化为罗马美德。

items.en: Old French equite carried the word into English, where it first meant fairness of judgment.
items.cn: 古法语 equite 把这个词带入英语，最初指判断的公正。

items.en: English law developed courts of equity to give remedies that the strict common law could not, and the word became the name of that system.
items.cn: 英国法发展出衡平法院，以提供严格普通法无法给出的救济，这个词便成为该体系的名称。

items.en: From the seventeenth century equity also named the owner's share in a venture, since a fair portion of value is a portion of ownership.
items.cn: 从十七世纪起，equity 也指所有者在事业中的份额，因为价值中应得的一份就是所有权的一份。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper origin): the pre-Latin origin of aequus is unsettled, and any Indo-European form offered for it is a reconstruction rather than a documented word.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：aequus 在拉丁语之前的来源无定论，凡为其给出的印欧形态均属重构，而非有书证的词。

note.en: Group one holds words built on the same level root; group two holds terms about fairness or ownership that answer a different question.
note.cn: 第一组是同出「均平」词根的词；第二组是关于公平或所有权的说法，回答的是不同问题。

entries.definition: Means identical shares or status; equity asks for fair shares, which may differ.
entries.definitionCN: 指份额或地位相同；equity 要求公平份额，份额可以不同。

entries.definition: Means fair or just; it describes a decision or arrangement, not a financial stake.
entries.definitionCN: 意为公平的、公正的，描述决定或安排，不指金融份额。

entries.definition: Unfairness or unjust difference; it is the opposite of the fairness sense, not of the financial one.
entries.definitionCN: 指不公平或不公正差异，是公平义的反面，而非金融义的反面。

entries.definition: Calmness of mind, from aequus plus animus 'mind'; it shares the root but has nothing to do with fairness.
entries.definitionCN: 指心境的平静，由 aequus 加 animus「心」构成；同根但与公平无关。

entries.definition: The everyday noun for just treatment; equity is its formal and legal counterpart.
entries.definitionCN: 指公正对待的日常名词；equity 是其正式与法律对应语。

entries.definition: A broader ideal of right order and law; equity often names a corrective within that order.
entries.definitionCN: 指正当秩序与法律的更宽理想；equity 常指该秩序内的矫正。

entries.definition: The fact or right of possessing something; equity in finance is a measured share of that right.
entries.definitionCN: 指拥有某物的事实或权利；金融中的 equity 是这一权利的可计量份额。

entries.definition: An interest or share in an enterprise; it is close to the financial sense but less technical.
entries.definitionCN: 指在事业中的利益或份额，接近金融义但较不技术化。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real related words, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实固定搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Latin aequus 'level' gives equity: first a level scale, then a fair share, then an ownership share.
normal.cn: 拉丁 aequus「平的」给出 equity：先指放平的秤，再指公平的一份，再指所有权份额。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the field: pay equity, equity stake, home equity, court of equity.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出领域：薪酬公平、股权、房屋净值、衡平法院。

normal.en: The family runs equitable, equitably, inequity, inequitable, equal and equality.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 equitable、equitably、inequity、inequitable、equal 与 equality。

normal.en: The same root appears in equator, equilibrium and equanimity, all built on the idea of level.
normal.cn: 同一词根见于 equator、equilibrium 与 equanimity，都建立在「平」的观念上。

normal.en: Finance pays equity last, which is why the word also carries risk.
normal.cn: 金融中权益最后受偿，因此这个词也带着风险。

abstract.en: Picture a scale adjusted so that the lighter side is not simply outvoted.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤被调整过，较轻的一边不会因分量小而直接被压过去。

abstract.en: Picture a deed that names who truly owns the house after every loan is counted.
abstract.cn: 想象一张契据，数清每笔贷款后写明谁真正拥有这栋房子。

abstract.en: Picture a court that can order someone to stop, not merely to pay.
abstract.cn: 想象一个法院能命令某人停手，而不只是让其赔钱。

examples.en: The scholarship fund was designed for equity, not for equal awards to every applicant.
examples.cn: 这项奖学金着眼于公平，而非给每位申请者相同金额。

examples.en: She sold half her equity in the startup to pay for the factory.
examples.cn: 她卖掉初创公司一半股权，用来支付工厂费用。

examples.en: The ruling came from a court of equity and stopped the eviction.
examples.cn: 这项裁决出自衡平法院，阻止了驱逐。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「equal（相等）+ ity（性质）」——把秤放平 → 公平；自己应得的那一份 → 权益

root: equity 经古法语来自拉丁 aequitas「均平、公正」，词根 aequus「平的、相等的」；aequus 更深来源不确定，凡更早形态均属重构。同根词包括 equal、equality、equator、equilibrium。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one level scale: fair treatment, an ownership share, net value, the law of fairness, equal-access policy, the residual financial claim, distributive justice and fair access to schooling.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一杆秤展开：公平对待、所有权份额、净值、衡平法、平权政策、剩余索取权、分配正义与教育机会公平。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a scale adjusted so that the lighter side is heard, not simply outweighed.
core.cn: 核心意象：一杆被调整过的秤，较轻的一边也能被听见，而不只是被压过去。

branches.en: FAIR SCALE: fairness of treatment and fairness of distribution are the same level scale writ large.
branches.cn: 公平的秤：对待公平与分配公平，是同一杆秤放大后的样子。

branches.en: OWNERSHIP: a fair share becomes a stake, and the last-paid claim carries the risk.
branches.cn: 所有权：公平的一份变成股份，最后受偿的主张承担风险。

branches.en: NET VALUE: accounting reduces the stake to the number left after debts.
branches.cn: 净值：会计把股份化约为清偿债务后剩下的数字。

branches.en: LEGAL REMEDY: the court of fairness can order a stop, not merely a payment.
branches.cn: 法律救济：公平法院能命令停手，而不只是判赔。

branches.en: ACCESS: policy removes barriers before the test rather than lowering the standard after it.
branches.cn: 机会：政策在考试前消除障碍，而非在考试后降低标准。

intro.en: The noun comes from the Latin word for evenness, and its derived adjectives and negatives keep the same root.
intro.cn: 这个名词来自拉丁语表示「均平」的词，其派生形容词与反义词延续同一词根。

latinIntro.en: Latin aequus and aequitas supply the root; English built equitable, equitably, inequity and equality on the same stock.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 aequus 与 aequitas 提供词根；英语在同一来源上造出 equitable、equitably、inequity 与 equality。

items.example: The root supplies the image of a level scale.
items.exampleCN: 这个词根提供水平秤的意象。

items.example: The ending turns the adjective into a noun.
items.exampleCN: 这个词尾把形容词变成名词。

items.example: Equity guided the relief.
items.exampleCN: 公平原则指导了救济。

items.example: The division was equitable.
items.exampleCN: 分配是公平的。

items.example: The funds were equitably shared.
items.exampleCN: 资金被公平分配。

items.example: The report found inequity in pay.
items.exampleCN: 报告发现薪酬不公。

items.example: Equality names identical status.
items.exampleCN: 平等指地位相同。

items.meaning: the level line around the earth
items.example: The equator divides the globe.
items.exampleCN: 赤道把地球分开。

items.example: The market reached equilibrium.
items.exampleCN: 市场达到平衡。

definition_zh: 资产；财富；优势
definition_en: something valuable that a person or company owns, or a useful quality
core_image: 账本左栏一件件能换成钱的东西
scene: 公司最值钱的不是机器，而是那批老客户。 Her calm voice is a great asset in court.
sceneCN: 这里 asset 是「优势」（第 2 个义项：能带来好处的人或特质）；句意是她在法庭上沉稳的嗓音是一大优势。

senses.title: Property of value
senses.definition: something of value owned by a person or a company
senses.definitionCN: 个人或公司拥有的、有价之物
senses.example: The company sold several assets to pay its debts.
senses.exampleCN: 公司卖掉几项资产来还债。
senses.why: Asset comes from Norman French asetz, 'enough to settle a debt', so the word began as property counted for its ability to pay.
senses.whyCN: asset 来自诺曼法语 asetz，原指「足以清偿债务的财产」，所以这个词一开始就是按「能抵债」来计量的财物。

senses.title: Useful quality or person
senses.definition: a person or quality that is useful and brings benefit
senses.definitionCN: 有用、能带来好处的人或特质
senses.example: Her calm voice is a great asset in court.
senses.exampleCN: 她在法庭上沉稳的嗓音是一大优势。
senses.why: Once anything that can pay off is counted as an asset, the step to a helpful person or trait is short: both are reckoned by the benefit they bring.
senses.whyCN: 凡是能抵用、能带来回报的东西都被算作资产，再向前一步，能帮上忙的人或特质也就成了资产，衡量标准都是「带来多少好处」。

intro.en: Asset is a Norman French word about having enough, and English turned it into a noun for property.
intro.cn: asset 是来自诺曼法语的词，本义与「足够」有关，英语把它变成表示财产的名词。

items.en: ad satis meant 'to enough', enough to meet a claim.
items.cn: ad satis 意为「达到足够」，即足以应付索偿。

items.en: asez meant 'enough, sufficiency of wealth'.
items.cn: asez 意为「足够、财富充裕」。

items.en: asetz named the property left by a debtor, enough to pay.
items.cn: asetz 指债务人留下的、足以偿债的财产。

items.en: English took assets as a plural noun for property and funds.
items.cn: 英语以复数形式 assets 借入，指财产与资金。

items.en: The sense widened to any valuable quality or helpful person.
items.cn: 词义扩大，凡有价值的特质或能帮忙的人也算资产。

note.en: The look-alike group is spelled like asset; the near-meaning group names property and advantage.
note.cn: 形近组拼写与 asset 相近；近义组是表示财产与优势的词。

entries.definition: to judge the value of
entries.definitionCN: 评估

entries.definition: to state firmly
entries.definitionCN: 断言

entries.definition: to agree
entries.definitionCN: 同意

entries.definition: things owned by someone
entries.definitionCN: 财产

entries.definition: something that helps or benefits
entries.definitionCN: 优势

entries.definition: a useful supply
entries.definitionCN: 资源

normalIntro.en: An asset is whatever can be counted on the left side of the ledger.
normalIntro.cn: 资产就是账本左栏里能数得出来的东西。

normal.en: The plural is far more common in finance: assets.
normal.cn: 在财务语境里复数形式更常见。

normal.en: It is a countable noun: a great asset, several assets.
normal.cn: 它是可数名词：一大优势、几项资产。

normal.en: One t in the middle, and stress falls on the first syllable: AS-set.
normal.cn: 中间只有一个 t，重音在第一个音节。

normal.en: The phrase be an asset to praises a person's value.
normal.cn: 短语 be an asset to 用来称赞某人的价值。

normal.en: Do not confuse it with assess, which is the verb.
normal.cn: 不要和动词 assess 混淆。

abstract.en: See a ledger page where each line can be turned into cash.
abstract.cn: 想象账本上每一行都能换成现金。

abstract.en: See a quiet colleague whose presence steadies a whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一位安静同事，他一来整个屋子就稳住了。

abstract.en: See a key that opens more than one door.
abstract.cn: 想象一把能开不止一扇门的钥匙。

examples.en: The company sold several assets to pay its debts.
examples.cn: 公司卖掉几项资产来还债。

examples.en: Her calm voice is a great asset in court.
examples.cn: 她在法庭上沉稳的嗓音是一大优势。

examples.en: Patience is an asset when you learn a language.
examples.cn: 学语言时，耐心是一种优势。

dict_mnemonic.text: 诺曼法语 asetz 本指「够还债的财产」，进入英语成 assets；从「能抵债的财物」引申为资产，再到「能帮忙的人或特质」。

root: 诺曼法语 asetz 意为「足以偿债的财产」，源自拉丁语 ad satis「达到足够」；由够还债的财物引申为资产，再抽象为能带来好处的优势。

sensesIntro.en: Property counted for what it can pay and a person counted for what they can give share one measure of value.
sensesIntro.cn: 财物按能抵多少债来算，人按能带来多少好处来算，用的是同一把价值尺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger line that can be turned into cash.
core.cn: 核心意象：账本上一行可以换成现金的条目。

branches.cn: 固定资产

branches.en: frozen assets
branches.cn: 冻结资产

branches.en: sell company assets
branches.cn: 出售公司资产

branches.en: a great asset
branches.cn: 一大优势

branches.en: an asset to the team
branches.cn: 队里的宝贵助力

intro.en: Asset is a borrowed whole word, but it sits in a wide field of property and value terms.
intro.cn: asset 是整体借入的词，但它处在一大片表示财产与价值的词场中。

latinIntro.en: Its Latin ancestor ad satis, 'to enough', also underlies satisfy and satiate.
latinIntro.cn: 它的拉丁语祖词 ad satis「达到足够」，也是 satisfy 与 satiate 的来源。

definition_zh: 审计；查账；审查，核查；税务稽查；（大学）旁听
definition_en: an official examination of accounts or of how something is done, or the act of making such an examination; in American universities, to attend a class without taking it for credit
core_image: 账本摊开，一笔笔念出来，旁边有人听着核对
scene: 年终结算前，会计把一摞凭证摊在长桌上，等外人来逐笔核对。 The firm hired an outside team to audit its accounts.
sceneCN: 这里 audit 是动词「审计、查账」（第 4 个义项）；句意是公司请外部团队来审计账目。

pos.zh: 及物动词：审计；核查；旁听

derivatives.zh: 同根加指人词尾：审计师；旁听生
动名词固化：审计工作；审计学
加否定前缀：未经审计的

senses.title: An official check of accounts
senses.definition: an official examination of the financial records of a company or person to confirm that they are accurate
senses.definitionCN: 对公司或个人的财务记录进行正式检查，以确认其准确无误
senses.example: The annual audit found two payments without receipts.
senses.exampleCN: 年度审计发现两笔付款没有收据。
senses.why: Accounts were once read aloud while an official listened and checked, so the noun still names a hearing of the books.
senses.whyCN: 从前账目要大声念出来，由官员听着核对，所以这个名词至今仍是「听账」的意思。

senses.title: A systematic review of practice
senses.definition: a structured examination of how a process, service or site meets a stated standard
senses.definitionCN: 对某个流程、服务或场所是否符合既定标准所作的系统性检查
senses.example: A safety audit closed the workshop for a week.
senses.exampleCN: 一次安全审查让车间停工了一周。
senses.why: The idea of an independent person checking against a rule transfers from money to any measurable practice.
senses.whyCN: 「由独立的人对照规则来核对」这一想法从钱款推广到任何可衡量的做法。

senses.title: A tax examination
senses.definition: an official check by the tax office of what a person or firm has declared
senses.definitionCN: 税务机关对申报内容进行的正式核查
senses.example: He kept every invoice in case of a tax audit.
senses.exampleCN: 他把每张发票都留着，以防税务稽查。
senses.why: The state is the listener who must be satisfied, so the same word names its inspection of your figures.
senses.whyCN: 国家就是那个必须被说服的「听者」，于是同一个词也指它对你数字的检查。

senses.title: To examine accounts officially
senses.definition: to examine financial records officially and report whether they are correct
senses.definitionCN: 正式检查财务记录并报告其是否正确
senses.example: An outside firm was asked to audit the accounts.
senses.exampleCN: 一家外部事务所受邀审计这些账目。
senses.why: The noun became a verb without changing form, keeping the picture of an outsider going through the books line by line.
senses.whyCN: 名词不经变形直接用作动词，保留了「外人逐行翻账」的画面。

senses.title: To review how something is done
senses.definition: to check a process, stock or performance against a standard and record the result
senses.definitionCN: 对照标准检查流程、库存或表现，并记录结果
senses.example: The team audited its own energy use.
senses.exampleCN: 团队核查了自己的能耗。
senses.why: Once the object need not be money, the verb simply means a disciplined check supported by evidence.
senses.whyCN: 一旦对象不必是钱款，这个动词就泛指有凭有据、按规矩做的检查。

senses.title: To attend a class without credit
senses.definition: to attend a university course without taking examinations or earning credit
senses.definitionCN: 在大学里听课但不参加考试、不取学分
senses.example: She audited a course in medieval history.
senses.exampleCN: 她旁听了一门中世纪史课程。
senses.why: American colleges kept the old sense of a listener present at a hearing: the student hears but is not examined.
senses.whyCN: 美国高校保留了「在场听审」的旧义：学生只是听，而不接受考核。

senses.title: A private stocktaking
senses.definition: a careful review of one's own habits, time or possessions
senses.definitionCN: 对自己的习惯、时间或物品所作的仔细清点
senses.example: A weekend audit of her subscriptions saved a lot of money.
senses.exampleCN: 周末对自己订阅服务的一次盘点省下了不少钱。
senses.why: The professional word lends its seriousness to private life, so any honest count of what is really there can be called an audit.
senses.whyCN: 专业词把它的严肃劲儿借给了私人生活，于是任何如实清点都可以叫这个名字。

intro.en: Audit belongs to the Latin hearing family: accounts were read aloud and an official listened, so checking the books is literally a hearing.
intro.cn: audit 属于拉丁语「听」词族：账目被大声宣读，由官员听着核对，所以查账在字面上就是一场「听审」。

items.en: The hearing family is generally traced to a root meaning to perceive, which combined with another element to give Latin audire; the reconstructed shape is debated.
items.cn: 「听」词族一般被认为出自表示「感知」的词根，与另一成分复合后产生拉丁语 audire；具体重构形式有争议。

items.en: Audire meant to hear, and its participle stem audit- supplied the nouns and adjectives of the family.
items.cn: audire 意为「听」，其分词词干 audit- 提供了这个词族的名词与形容词。

items.en: Auditus named a hearing or listening, and in administration it came to mean the hearing of accounts.
items.cn: auditus 指「听、倾听」这一行为，在行政语境中引申为「听取账目」。

items.en: Accounts were read aloud before an official who listened and questioned the steward, because many people present could not read.
items.cn: 账目要在官员面前大声宣读，由他听着并向管家质询，因为在场许多人并不识字。

items.en: English took the word in the fifteenth century for an official examination of accounts, and later used it as a verb.
items.cn: 英语在十五世纪借入这个词，指对账目的正式检查，后来又用作动词。

items.en: The noun spread to safety, quality and energy checks, while American colleges kept the verb for sitting in a class without credit.
items.cn: 这个名词扩展到安全、质量与能耗检查，而美国高校则保留「旁听」这一动词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group stays inside the Latin hearing family, with one false friend; the near-meaning group grades kinds of checking.
note.cn: 形近组留在拉丁语「听」词族内部，并掺入一个假朋友；近义组按检查的种类分级。

entries.definition: the person who carries out an audit
entries.definitionCN: 执行审计的人；同根，多了指人的词尾。

entries.definition: relating to the sense of hearing
entries.definitionCN: 听觉的；同根形容词，回到「听」的本义。

entries.definition: a trial performance heard by judges
entries.definitionCN: 试演；同根，指让评委「听」的一次表演。

entries.definition: bold or reckless
entries.definitionCN: 大胆的；只是拼写相近，出自「敢」的词根，与「听」无关。

entries.definition: a close look at something to check its condition
entries.definitionCN: 检查；侧重实地查看状况，不一定查账。

entries.definition: a general reconsideration of work or records
entries.definitionCN: 复核；比审计宽泛，未必有正式结论。

entries.definition: close and careful examination
entries.definitionCN: 细察；强调看得仔细，不含出具报告之意。

entries.definition: the act of confirming that something is true
entries.definitionCN: 核实；确认某事为真，范围比审计小。

normalIntro.en: Audit is a hearing of the books: someone reads, someone listens, and the numbers must answer.
normalIntro.cn: audit 是一场「听账」：有人念，有人听，数字必须对得上。

normal.en: The stem audit- comes from the Latin verb for hear.
normal.cn: 词干 audit- 出自拉丁语表示「听」的动词。

normal.en: Auditor, auditory and audition share the same stem.
normal.cn: auditor、auditory、audition 共用同一词干。

normal.en: An audit ends in a report, not just a look.
normal.cn: 审计以报告收尾，不只是看一眼。

normal.en: To audit a class is to hear it without credit.
normal.cn: 旁听课程就是只听课、不拿学分。

normal.en: Audacious only looks similar; it comes from a root for daring.
normal.cn: audacious 只是形近，它出自「敢」的词根。

abstract.en: Picture a ledger read aloud in a stone hall.
abstract.cn: 想象账本在石厅里被大声念出来。

abstract.en: Picture two columns, one read and one ticked.
abstract.cn: 想象两栏数字，一栏念、一栏打钩。

abstract.en: Picture a student at the back who never sits an exam.
abstract.cn: 想象一个坐在后排、从不参加考试的学生。

examples.en: The audit revealed a gap in the petty cash.
examples.cn: 审计发现零用现金有一处缺口。

examples.en: An outside firm will audit the accounts this spring.
examples.cn: 今年春天将由一家外部事务所审计账目。

examples.en: She audited two lectures a week and took no exams.
examples.cn: 她每周旁听两节课，不参加考试。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：audi「听」加 -t——账目念给专人听、逐笔核对，就是审计；只听课不考试，就是旁听。

root: 拉丁语 audire「听」的分词词干 audit- 构成 auditus「听、听审」；中世纪账目口头宣读核对的做法使它专指查账，十五世纪进入英语，后扩展为各类系统审查，美式英语又保留旁听义。

sensesIntro.en: From a hearing of accounts the word spreads to any evidenced check, then turns into a verb, and finally names the listener who sits in a class.
sensesIntro.cn: 从「听账」出发，这个词扩展到任何有凭有据的检查，再转为动词，最后落到坐在教室里只听不考的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ledger read aloud while a listener ticks each line
core.cn: 核心意象：账本被大声念出，听的人逐行打钩

branches.en: accounts and tax declarations checked
branches.cn: 账目与纳税申报被核对

branches.en: a safety or quality review
branches.cn: 安全或质量审查

branches.en: the verb: go through books or processes
branches.cn: 动词：查账或核查流程

branches.en: a listener without credit
branches.cn: 不取学分的旁听者

branches.en: a private stocktaking of habits
branches.cn: 对习惯的私人盘点

intro.en: The stem audit- means heard; from it English builds the person, the adjective, the place and the act of hearing.
intro.cn: 词干 audit- 意为「被听到的」，英语由此造出指人、指性质、指场所与指行为的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin audire, to hear, gives auditus, auditor, auditorium and audibilis, the last of which became audible.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 audire「听」产生 auditus、auditor、auditorium 与 audibilis，最后一个成了英语的「听得见的」。

items.example: audible, audience
items.exampleCN: 听得见的；听众

items.example: an annual audit
items.exampleCN: 年度审计

items.example: an external auditor
items.exampleCN: 外部审计师

items.example: the auditory nerve
items.exampleCN: 听神经

items.example: a school auditorium
items.exampleCN: 学校礼堂

items.example: an open audition

items.example: barely audible

items.example: an inaudible whisper
items.exampleCN: 听不见的耳语

items.example: unaudited figures
items.exampleCN: 未经审计的数字

items.example: an auditable trail
items.exampleCN: 可审计的记录链

latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个动词是整个词族的源头。
这个名词后来成了查账。

latinEntries.example: Auditor already meant an official listener.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 这个词在拉丁语里已指官方听审者。
这个名词产生了英语的「听众」。

definition_zh: 采购；（机构）取得货物与服务的过程；获得
definition_en: the process by which an organization obtains goods and services, or the act of obtaining something
core_image: 一张需求单从部门递出，经过比价与签约，最后变成仓库门口的一批货
scene: 需求单在几个部门之间传了一轮，几份报价摊在桌上，最后一份合同签下，货物才被允许进门。 Public procurement must follow open tendering rules.
sceneCN: 需求、比价、签约三道手续走完，货物才被允许进门；句中的 procurement 指「机构取得货物与服务的整个采购过程」（第 1 个义项：从提出需求到签订合同、完成交付的流程）。图中可辨识物件：需求单、报价单、合同、仓库门。

senses.title: An organization's buying process
senses.titleCN: 机构取得货物与服务的采购流程
senses.definition: the whole process by which an organization obtains the goods and services it needs
senses.definitionCN: 机构为取得所需货物与服务而走的整个流程
senses.example: Public procurement must follow open tendering rules.
senses.exampleCN: 政府采购必须遵守公开招标规则。
senses.why: the word began as a term for managing affairs on someone's behalf, and buying is the part of that care that leaves a paper trail.
senses.whyCN: 这个词原指替他人料理事务，而采购正是这种照料中会留下纸面痕迹的那一部分。

senses.title: The purchasing department
senses.definition: the department or team responsible for buying on behalf of the organization
senses.definitionCN: 代表机构负责采购的部门或团队
senses.example: Procurement blocked the order until three quotes arrived.
senses.exampleCN: 采购部门压住订单，直到收到三份报价。
senses.why: the process gave its name to the unit that runs it, a common shift in institutional language.
senses.whyCN: 流程把名字给了执行它的单位，这是机构用语中常见的转称。

senses.title: Government buying
senses.titleCN: 以公共资金进行的政府采购
senses.definition: the purchase of goods and works by public bodies with public money
senses.definitionCN: 公共机构用公共资金购买货物与工程
senses.example: Government procurement is opened to foreign bidders.
senses.exampleCN: 政府采购向外国投标者开放。
senses.why: public money requires rules of fairness, so the general word is paired with the word for the state.
senses.whyCN: 公共资金要求公平规则，因此一般词前面加上了指国家的词。

senses.title: Military supply acquisition
senses.titleCN: 军需物资与装备的采购
senses.definition: the obtaining of weapons, supplies and services for armed forces
senses.definitionCN: 为武装部队取得武器、物资与服务
senses.example: Defence procurement ran years behind the schedule.
senses.exampleCN: 国防采购比计划晚了数年。
senses.why: armed forces buy in secret and at scale, so their buying developed its own vocabulary around the same word.
senses.whyCN: 军队的秘密大批采购使同一词在其内部发展出专门说法。

senses.title: Buying through digital systems
senses.titleCN: 通过电子系统完成的采购
senses.definition: the use of online platforms and systems to buy goods and services
senses.definitionCN: 利用网络平台与系统购买货物与服务
senses.example: E-procurement cut the order cycle from weeks to days.
senses.exampleCN: 电子采购把订单周期从数周缩短到数日。
senses.why: the channel changed, not the act, so a short prefix marks the electronic form.
senses.whyCN: 变的是渠道而不是行为，因此只用一个短前缀标出电子形式。

senses.title: Buying with environmental criteria
senses.titleCN: 把环境标准纳入评审的绿色采购
senses.definition: buying that includes environmental and social conditions in its award criteria
senses.definitionCN: 在评标标准中纳入环境与社会条件的采购
senses.example: Green procurement favoured recycled paper and low-emission vans.
senses.exampleCN: 绿色采购偏向再生纸与低排放货车。
senses.why: when price is no longer the only measure, an adjective is added to the same process.
senses.whyCN: 当价格不再是唯一尺度时，只需在同一流程前加一个形容词。

senses.title: Obtaining something in general
senses.titleCN: 正式用语中一般的「取得、获得」
senses.definition: the obtaining of something abstract, such as funds or evidence
senses.definitionCN: 取得某种抽象之物，如资金或证据
senses.example: The procurement of funds delayed the whole project.
senses.exampleCN: 资金迟迟未能取得，拖住了整个项目。
senses.why: the older and wider sense survives in formal prose, where what is obtained need not be goods.
senses.whyCN: 较旧而较宽的含义留在正式文体中，被取得的东西不一定是货物。

senses.title: Buying as a strategic choice
senses.titleCN: 作为战略决策的采购（自制或外购）
senses.definition: the strategic decision about what to make in house and what to buy outside
senses.definitionCN: 决定什么自己做、什么向外部购买的策略选择
senses.example: Procurement now sits at the table when products are designed.
senses.exampleCN: 如今产品设计时，采购部门也坐在桌边。
senses.why: once buying is planned rather than clerical, it becomes a lever on cost, risk and design.
senses.whyCN: 当采购从文书工作变成事先规划，它就成了影响成本、风险与设计的杠杆。

intro.en: Procurement comes through Old French from Latin procurare 'to take care of, attend to', built on pro- 'for' and curare 'to care for'. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: procurement 经古法语来自拉丁语 procurare「照料、料理」，由表示「为了、代表」的前缀与 curare「关心、照料」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: Cura meant 'care, concern, careful attention', and it also lies behind cure, accurate and curious.
items.cn: cura 意为「关心、忧虑、仔细留意」，它也是「治愈」「准确的」「好奇的」等词的根源。

items.en: Curare 'to care for, look after, attend to' is the verb formed from cura.
items.cn: curare「照料、看护、料理」是由 cura 构成的动词。

items.en: Pro- 'for, on behalf of' plus curare gave procurare 'to take care of something for someone, to manage'.
items.cn: 表示「为了、代表」的前缀加 curare 构成 procurare「替某人料理某事、管理」。

items.en: Old French procurer meant 'to manage, take care of, obtain', and English borrowed it in the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 古法语 procurer 意为「管理、照料、取得」，英语在十四世纪借入。

items.en: The noun first meant management or the care of affairs, and only later narrowed to the obtaining of supplies.
items.cn: 这个名词最初指管理或料理事务，后来才收窄为取得物资。

items.en: In the twentieth century the word settled on formal institutional buying, with tenders, contracts and audit trails.
items.cn: 到二十世纪，这个词固定指机构的正式采购，伴随招标、合同与审计记录。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same 'care' root whose meanings have diverged; group two holds words for buying.
note.cn: 第一组同出「关心、照料」这一词根，意义已各自分化；第二组是表示购买的词。

entries.definition: To obtain something, often with effort; the noun names the organized process that does it.
entries.definitionCN: 取得某物，常需费一番功夫；名词指把这件事组织起来的流程。

entries.definition: An official who acts on another's behalf, from the same root; it kept the old sense of managing for someone.
entries.definitionCN: 代表他人行事的官员，同出该词根；保留了「替人管理」的旧义。

entries.definition: Built from the prefix for 'to' plus the care verb: something done carefully, hence exact.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示「朝向」的前缀加「照料」动词构成：仔细做成，因此精确。

entries.definition: From the same care noun: originally 'careful, attentive', later 'eager to know'.
entries.definitionCN: 同出该「关心」名词：原为「仔细、留意」，后转指「想知道」。

entries.definition: The routine buying of goods; procurement adds planning, competition and formal rules.
entries.definitionCN: 日常的货物购买；procurement 另有规划、竞争与正式规则之意。

entries.definition: The obtaining of something, often an asset or a company; it says nothing about tendering.
entries.definitionCN: 取得某物，常指资产或公司；并不涉及招标程序。

entries.definition: The search for and selection of suppliers, the front half of procurement.
entries.definitionCN: 寻找并挑选供应商，是采购流程的前半段。

entries.definition: The providing of goods to those who need them, seen from the giving side rather than the buying side.
entries.definitionCN: 向需要者提供货物，站在给予方而非购买方来看。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the real 'care' root, the real institutional phrases and the real family.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用真实的「照料」词根、真实的机构搭配与真实词族。

normal.en: The root means 'care': procurement is buying done with care and on paper.
normal.cn: 词根意为「照料」：采购就是带着小心、留下纸面记录的购买。

normal.en: The family runs procure, procurable, procurer and procuration.
normal.cn: 同族词包括采购、可取得的、取得者与代理办理。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark it: public procurement, procurement process, procurement officer.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出这个词：政府采购、采购流程、采购主管。

normal.en: The same care root gives accurate and curious, both once meaning careful.
normal.cn: 同一「照料」词根还给出「准确的」与「好奇的」，两者都曾表示「仔细」。

normal.en: Procurement begins with a need and ends with a signed contract.
normal.cn: 采购从一项需求开始，到一份签好的合同结束。

abstract.en: Picture a request form travelling through three desks before it becomes a crate.
abstract.cn: 想象一张需求单走过三张办公桌，最后变成一只货箱。

abstract.en: Picture a scale that weighs not goods but promises.
abstract.cn: 想象一杆秤，称的不是货物，而是承诺。

abstract.en: Picture a gardener who plans what to bring in before winter.
abstract.cn: 想象一位园丁，在入冬前就盘算好要备进什么。

examples.en: Procurement rules require at least three competing bids.
examples.cn: 采购规则要求至少三家竞标报价。

examples.en: The hospital's procurement of masks began before the outbreak.
examples.cn: 这家医院在疫情暴发前就已采购口罩。

examples.en: She moved from procurement into supply-chain planning.
examples.cn: 她从采购转到供应链规划。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「pro（为了）+ cure（关心）+ ment」——为机构所需之事操心办理 → 采购

root: 古法语 procurement 来自拉丁语 procurare（照料、料理、管理）＝pro-（为了、代表）＋curare（关心、照料），词根 cura 意为「关心」。原义为管理事务，后收窄为采购。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from caring for an institution's affairs and narrow into the paper process of buying, which then spreads to government, defence, digital systems and strategy.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「替机构料理事务」出发，收窄为有纸面流程的购买，再扩展到政府、国防、数字系统与战略。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a request form that becomes a signed contract and then a crate at the door.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张需求单变成一份签好的合同，再变成门口的一只货箱。

branches.en: THE PROCESS AND ITS OFFICE: a way of caring for needs hardens into a department.
branches.cn: 流程与其部门：照料需求的方式固定为一个部门。

branches.en: PUBLIC AND ARMED BUYING: public money and secrecy each add their own rules.
branches.cn: 公共与军事购买：公共资金与保密各自添上一套规则。

branches.en: NEW CRITERIA: a digital channel and environmental scoring change how the same act is done.
branches.cn: 新标准：数字渠道与环境评分改变的是同一行为的做法。

branches.en: WIDER OBTAINING: the old sense survives where what is obtained is funds or evidence.
branches.cn: 更宽的取得：旧义留在取得资金或证据的场合。

branches.en: AT THE DESIGN TABLE: buying becomes a decision about what not to make.
branches.cn: 坐上设计桌：采购成了决定「不做什么」的决策。

intro.en: The word is a Latin prefix, a Latin noun of care and its verb, plus a French noun ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由一个拉丁前缀、一个表「关心」的拉丁名词及其动词，再加一个法语名词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin cura gives cure, accurate and curious as well as procure and procurement.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 cura 除构成「采购」一族外，还给出「治愈」「准确的」「好奇的」等词。

items.example: The prefix says the care is exercised for someone else.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀说明照料是替别人做的。

items.example: The noun names the attention being given.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词指所付出的留意。

items.structure: curare, curavi, curatum (Latin verb, first conjugation)
items.example: The verb turns care into an activity.
items.exampleCN: 这个动词把「关心」变成行动。

items.example: Procurare is the source of the English family.
items.exampleCN: 这个词是英语这一词族的来源。

items.example: They procured the parts within a week.
items.exampleCN: 他们一周内就取得了零件。

items.example: Procurement takes months for large works.
items.exampleCN: 大型工程的采购要花几个月。

items.example: The rare alloy was no longer procurable.
items.exampleCN: 那种稀有合金已无法采购到。

items.example: The procurer dealt with every supplier.
items.exampleCN: 采购者与每一家供应商打交道。

items.example: The count was accurate to the last crate.
items.exampleCN: 清点精确到最后一箱。

definition_zh: 温柔的；嫩的；疼痛的；正式提出；投标；照管者
definition_en: gentle and careful; easily painful; or to offer something formally; also a formal offer or a caregiver
core_image: 碰一下就皱眉的嫩芽，也是递出标书时轻放的手
scene: 照看幼苗的人连浇水都放轻了手。 The young plants need tender care in the first weeks.
sceneCN: 这里 tender 是形容词「精心呵护的、温柔的」（第 1 个义项：温柔体贴的）；句意：幼苗头几周需要温柔细致的照料。

derivatives.zh: 温柔地（形容词加 -ly 构成）
温柔；触痛（形容词加 -ness 构成）
使肉变嫩（形容词加 -ize 动词后缀）

senses.title: Gentle, loving and careful
senses.definition: showing gentleness, kindness and care
senses.definitionCN: 表现出温柔、善意与呵护
senses.example: She gave the rescued kitten tender care.
senses.exampleCN: 她悉心照料获救的小猫。
senses.why: The image is the young shoot: what is soft needs and receives a soft touch.
senses.whyCN: 意象是嫩芽：柔弱之物需要也召来轻柔的触碰。

senses.title: Soft and easy to cut or chew
senses.definition: soft and easy to bite, used of meat or plants
senses.definitionCN: 柔软易咬的，用于肉或植物
senses.example: Slow cooking makes the beef tender.
senses.exampleCN: 慢炖使牛肉软嫩。
senses.why: Physical softness is the literal shoot image: tender flesh yields to the touch.
senses.whyCN: 物理的柔嫩是「嫩芽」意象的直取：嫩肉一按即让。

senses.title: Painful when touched
senses.definition: sensitive or painful to touch, used of skin or muscles
senses.definitionCN: 触碰即痛，用于皮肤或肌肉
senses.example: The bruise is still tender.
senses.exampleCN: 淤伤一按还疼。
senses.why: The shoot also flinches: what is soft hurts when pressed.
senses.whyCN: 嫩芽也会躲闪：柔弱之处一经按压便喊疼。

senses.title: To offer something formally
senses.definition: to present something officially, such as a resignation or a bid
senses.definitionCN: 正式呈递某物，如辞呈或标书
senses.example: He tendered his resignation this morning.
senses.exampleCN: 他今早正式递交辞呈。
senses.why: A formal offer is handled with both hands, gently placed: the same soft touch, now ceremonial.
senses.whyCN: 正式呈递之物以双手轻放：同一种轻柔触碰，只是此番带上仪式感。

senses.title: A formal offer or bid
senses.definition: a written offer to do work or supply goods at a fixed price
senses.definitionCN: 按定价承接工程或供货的书面报价
senses.example: Five companies submitted tenders for the bridge.
senses.exampleCN: 五家公司提交了大桥工程投标。
senses.why: The offer itself is named by the gesture: the placed document is a tender.
senses.whyCN: 报价以那个动作命名：被轻轻放上桌的文件，就叫 tender。

senses.title: A person or boat that attends another
senses.titleCN: 照管者；随侍人员；补给船
senses.definition: a person or small boat that serves or attends to a larger one
senses.definitionCN: 照看他人或为主船服务的小船或人员
senses.example: The bar tender kept everyone's glasses full.
senses.exampleCN: 酒吧侍者让大家的杯子一直满着。
senses.why: The one who tends is named after the care itself: attendance is tenderness in work clothes.
senses.whyCN: 照管者以「照料」为名：随侍就是穿上工装的温柔。

intro.en: English has two tenders. The soft one comes from Latin tener, delicate, through Old French tendre. The offer one comes from tendere, to stretch toward, the same root as tend.

items.en: Tener meant delicate, soft, young; its deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: tener 意为柔嫩、幼小；其更深词根不确定。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch toward, and its participle tensus gives tense.
items.cn: tendere 意为朝某方向拉伸，分词 tensus 生成 tense。

items.en: Old French tendre carried both Latin words, soft and stretching, into English.
items.cn: 古法语 tendre 把拉丁两词——柔嫩与拉伸——一并带入英语。

items.en: English borrowed tendre twice: the soft adjective and the offer verb.
items.cn: 英语两度借入 tendre：柔嫩的形容词与呈递的动词。

definition_zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占
definition_en: exclusive control of a market or commodity by a single seller
core_image: 一条街只有一家店开门，橱窗上贴着唯一的价目表，顾客排成长队也别无选择
scene: 小镇上唯一的一家加油站挂出新的价目牌，排队的车主只能接受。 A local monopoly can raise prices until customers travel to a distant substitute.
sceneCN: 这里 monopoly 指「由单一卖方控制的市场结构」（第 1 个义项：市场上只有一个卖方）；句意为地方性垄断可以把价格提高，直到顾客愿意去远处寻找替代品。图中可辨识物件：唯一的加油站、单一价目牌、排队车辆、远处的替代站点。

pos.zh: 垄断；垄断企业；专卖权；独占

senses.title: A market with one seller
senses.definition: a market structure in which a single seller supplies the whole demand and faces no direct rival
senses.definitionCN: 由单一卖方供应全部需求、没有直接对手的市场结构
senses.example: The island's ferry service is a monopoly with no alternative route.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的渡轮服务是一种没有替代航线的垄断。
senses.why: monos 'single' plus polein 'sell' gives the literal reading: one seller for the whole market.
senses.whyCN: monos「单一」加 polein「卖」给出字面读法：整个市场只有一个卖方。

senses.title: An exclusive right granted by law
senses.definition: a legal privilege allowing one party alone to trade in a good or service
senses.definitionCN: 允许某一方独自经营某种商品或服务的法定特权
senses.example: The old charter gave the company a monopoly on salt.
senses.exampleCN: 旧特许状给了这家公司食盐的专营权。
senses.why: the Greek word first named a concession granted by a city, so the legal sense is older than the economic one.
senses.whyCN: 这个希腊词最初指城邦授予的特许，因此法律义比经济义更早。

senses.title: The commodity under exclusive control
senses.definition: the good or service that only one supplier is allowed or able to provide
senses.definitionCN: 只允许或只能够由一家供应商提供的商品或服务
senses.example: Broadcasting was once a monopoly of the state.
senses.exampleCN: 广播曾经是国家独占的事业。
senses.why: English allows the word to stand for the thing controlled, not only for the control itself.
senses.whyCN: 英语允许这个词指被控制的对象，而不只是控制本身。

senses.title: The firm that holds the market
senses.definition: the company or organization that enjoys exclusive control
senses.definitionCN: 享有独占控制权的公司或机构
senses.example: Regulators treated the railway as a monopoly and capped its fares.
senses.exampleCN: 监管者把这家铁路公司当作垄断企业，并限制其票价。
senses.why: metonymy turns the structure into the actor, so monopoly can mean the monopolist.
senses.whyCN: 转喻把结构变成行为者，于是 monopoly 可以指垄断企业。

senses.title: A state monopoly
senses.definition: exclusive government control of a trade, often for revenue or public order
senses.definitionCN: 政府对某项贸易的独占控制，常用于增加财政收入或维护公共秩序
senses.example: The tobacco monopoly supplies a large share of the budget.
senses.exampleCN: 烟草专卖提供了预算的很大一部分。
senses.why: early modern states used exclusive grants as a tax-collecting device, and the phrase kept that association.
senses.whyCN: 近代早期国家把专营特许当作征税工具，这个说法保留了这层联系。

senses.title: A temporary monopoly from a patent
senses.titleCN: 专利或版权带来的暂时独占
senses.definition: exclusive commercial use of an invention or work for a limited term
senses.definitionCN: 在有限期限内对某项发明或作品的独占商业使用
senses.example: The patent gave the maker a monopoly for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 专利给了制造商二十年的独占期。
senses.why: intellectual property is a deliberate, time-limited monopoly meant to reward disclosure.
senses.whyCN: 知识产权是一种有意设置、期限有限的垄断，用以奖励公开。

senses.title: A natural monopoly
senses.definition: a market where high fixed costs make one supplier cheaper than several
senses.definitionCN: 固定成本很高、使一家供应比多家供应更便宜的市场
senses.example: Water pipes form a natural monopoly because duplicating them is wasteful.
senses.exampleCN: 水管构成自然垄断，因为重复铺设是浪费。
senses.why: economists call it natural because the single supplier arises from cost structure, not from a legal grant.
senses.whyCN: 经济学家称之为「自然」，因为单一供应来自成本结构，而非法律授予。

senses.title: Exclusive possession of anything
senses.titleCN: 对任何事物的排他性掌控（比喻义）
senses.definition: complete control of a thing or topic so that others have no share
senses.definitionCN: 对某事物或话题的完全控制，使他人无从分享
senses.example: The city does not have a monopoly on good ideas.
senses.exampleCN: 好主意并非这座城市所独占。
senses.why: detached from trade, the word keeps only its core of being the sole holder.
senses.whyCN: 脱离贸易语境后，这个词只保留「唯一持有者」这一核心。

intro.en: Monopoly comes from Greek monopōlion 'exclusive right to sell', built on monos 'alone' and pōlein 'to sell', and enters English through Latin monopolium. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: monopoly 来自希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」，由 monos「单独」与 pōlein「卖」构成，经拉丁 monopolium 进入英语。年代均为约数。

items.en: Monos meant 'alone, single'. The same element opens monologue, monorail and monarchy, where it combines with different second terms.
items.cn: monos 意为「单独的、唯一的」。同一成分出现在 monologue、monorail 与 monarchy 的开头，与不同的第二成分组合。

items.en: Pōlein meant 'to sell'. The -poly of monopoly is this verb, not Greek polys 'many', and it has nothing to do with polis 'city'.
items.cn: pōlein 意为「卖」。monopoly 中的 -poly 是这个动词，而非希腊语 polys「多」，也与 polis「城邦」无关。

items.en: Monopōlion named an exclusive sale or a concession granted by a city, especially the right to sell a particular commodity.
items.cn: monopōlion 指独家售卖或城邦授予的特许，尤其是经营某种商品的专权。

items.en: Latin took the Greek noun as monopolium and used it for exclusive trading rights, including grants made by rulers.
items.cn: 拉丁语把希腊名词吸收为 monopolium，用于独家贸易权，包括统治者授予的特许。

items.en: English borrowed the word in the sixteenth century, first for royal grants and later for any single-seller market as economics developed.
items.cn: 英语在 16 世纪借入这个词，先指王室特许，随着经济学发展又指任何单一卖方市场。

items.en: The exact first English citation is approximate. The deeper origin of pōlein is reconstructed rather than attested.
items.cn: 最早的英语书证年代只是约数。pōlein 的更深来源属重构形式，并非有直接书证。

note.en: Group one holds neighbouring market structures whose Greek second elements are often confused; group two holds words for control or exclusive dealing that are not market structures.
note.cn: 第一组是第二成分常被混淆的邻近市场结构；第二组是表示控制或独家交易、但并非市场结构的词。

entries.definition: A market with a single buyer; its Greek second element is opsōnein 'to buy', so it is the mirror image of monopoly.
entries.definitionCN: 只有一个买方的市场；其希腊第二成分是 opsōnein「买」，因此是 monopoly 的镜像。

entries.definition: A market dominated by a small number of sellers; the second element is the same verb 'to sell', but the first is oligos 'few'.
entries.definitionCN: 由少数卖方支配的市场；第二成分同为「卖」这个动词，但第一成分是 oligos「少数」。

entries.definition: A market with two dominant sellers, built with Latin duo- on the same Greek selling element.
entries.definitionCN: 由两家主要卖方构成的市场，以拉丁 duo- 接同一个希腊「卖」成分。

entries.definition: The person or firm that holds a monopoly; the structure is monopoly, while the holder is the monopolist.
entries.definitionCN: 持有垄断地位的人或企业；结构是 monopoly，持有者则是 monopolist。

entries.definition: To gain control of a commodity by buying enough of it to dictate price; it is an action, not a market structure.
entries.definitionCN: 通过买下足够多的商品来控制价格；它是一种行为，而非市场结构。

entries.definition: The state of being restricted to one party; a monopoly is one legal or economic form of exclusivity.
entries.definitionCN: 仅限一方享有的状态；垄断是排他性的一种法律或经济形式。

entries.definition: An agreement among independent sellers to fix prices or divide markets; it imitates monopoly without a single seller.
entries.definitionCN: 独立卖方之间固定价格或划分市场的协议；它模仿垄断，却没有单一卖方。

entries.definition: In late nineteenth-century law, a trust was a combination of firms placed under shared trustees, the target of early antitrust law.
entries.definitionCN: 在 19 世纪后期的法律中，trust 指置于共同受托人下的企业联合，是早期反垄断法的对象。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: monos 'single' + polein 'sell': one seller for the whole market.
normal.cn: monos「单一」+ polein「卖」：整个市场只有一个卖方。

normal.en: The family runs monopoly, monopolist, monopolize, monopolistic, monopolization.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 monopoly、monopolist、monopolize、monopolistic、monopolization。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the market sense: natural monopoly, state monopoly, monopoly power.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出市场义：自然垄断、国家专卖、垄断力量。

normal.en: The -poly here is 'sell', not 'many': oligopoly and duopoly use the same verb.
normal.cn: 这里的 -poly 是「卖」而非「多」：oligopoly 与 duopoly 用的是同一个动词。

normal.en: Its mirror image is monopsony, where one buyer faces many sellers.
normal.cn: 它的镜像是 monopsony，即一个买方面对许多卖方。

abstract.en: Picture a street with one lit window and a queue outside it.
abstract.cn: 想象一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，门外排着队。

abstract.en: Picture a single key that opens every door in a building.
abstract.cn: 想象一把钥匙能打开一栋楼里的每一扇门。

abstract.en: Picture one price tag that nobody on the street can undercut.
abstract.cn: 想象一张街上无人能压低的价签。

examples.en: The government broke up the monopoly after a decade of complaints.
examples.cn: 在十年投诉之后，政府拆分了这家垄断企业。

examples.en: A patent is a legal monopoly limited in time and scope.
examples.cn: 专利是一种在时间与范围上受限的法定垄断。

examples.en: No single company should have a monopoly on the public record.
examples.cn: 不应由任何一家公司独占公共记录。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「mono（单一）+ poly（卖）」——整个市场只有一家在卖 → 垄断

root: 希腊 monos「单独」+ pōlein「卖」→ 希腊 monopōlion「独家售卖权」→ 拉丁 monopolium → 英语 monopoly。此处的 -poly 是「卖」，与 polys「多」及 polis「城邦」无关。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one seller: a single hand holds the whole supply, and that hold is then seen as a market structure, a legal grant, the commodity, the firm, a state trade, a patent term, a cost-driven case, and finally any exclusive possession.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个卖方展开：一只手握住全部供给，这个握有再依次被视为市场结构、法律授予、被控商品、企业本身、国家贸易、专利期限、成本造成的特例，最后是任何排他性占有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one lit shop window on a street, with a queue that has nowhere else to go.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上只有一扇亮着的橱窗，队伍无处可去。

branches.en: STRUCTURE AND ACTOR: the single-seller market, and the firm that occupies it.
branches.cn: 结构与行为者：单一卖方市场，以及占据它的企业。

branches.en: GRANT AND OBJECT: a legal privilege, and the commodity that privilege covers.
branches.cn: 授予与对象：一项法律特权，以及该特权覆盖的商品。

branches.en: THE STATE: the same exclusive hold exercised for revenue or order.
branches.cn: 国家：为财政收入或秩序行使的同一种独占。

branches.en: TIME-LIMITED AND COST-DRIVEN: a patent term, and a market where fixed costs favour one supplier.
branches.cn: 限期与成本驱动：专利期限，以及固定成本偏向单一卖方的市场。

branches.en: ANY EXCLUSIVE HOLD: the word detached from trade and used for ideas or records.
branches.cn: 任何独占：脱离贸易后被用于思想或记录的词。

intro.en: Monopoly is a Greek compound filtered through Latin, so its two Greek elements can be read apart, and English then built a whole family on the noun.
intro.cn: monopoly 是经拉丁语过滤的希腊复合词，因此两个希腊成分可以分开读，英语随后又在这个名词上建起整个词族。

latinIntro.en: Latin monopolium carries the Greek compound into English; the family then adds -ist, -ize and -ation, while monopsony replaces the selling element with a buying one.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 monopolium 把这个希腊复合词带入英语；词族随后加 -ist、-ize 与 -ation，而 monopsony 把「卖」的成分换成「买」。

items.example: The element also opens monologue and monorail.
items.exampleCN: 这个成分也出现在 monologue 与 monorail 的开头。

items.example: The selling element is shared by oligopoly and duopoly.
items.exampleCN: 这个「卖」的成分由 oligopoly 与 duopoly 共享。

items.example: A local monopoly raised prices without fear.
items.exampleCN: 一家地方垄断者无所顾忌地提价。

items.example: The monopolist owned every pipeline in the valley.
items.exampleCN: 这家垄断企业拥有谷地里的每一条管道。

items.example: The monopolistic pricing drew regulatory attention.
items.exampleCN: 垄断定价引起了监管注意。

items.example: One firm monopolized the supply of spare parts.
items.exampleCN: 一家企业独占了备件供应。

items.example: Monopolization of the route took only three years.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线的垄断化只用了三年。

items.example: A monopsony can push purchase prices down.
items.exampleCN: 买方垄断可以把收购价压低。

items.example: The route is a duopoly of two airlines.
items.exampleCN: 这条航线是两家航空公司的双寡头。

items.example: An oligopoly kept prices stable for years.
items.exampleCN: 寡头格局让价格多年保持稳定。

definition_zh: 消费者；用户
definition_en: a person who buys goods or services for their own use
core_image: 超市里推着购物车、逐件比较价签的人
scene: 超市里，一位顾客拿着两瓶洗衣液比价。 Every consumer has the right to clear information.
sceneCN: 这里 consumer 指「消费者」（第 1 个义项：购买并使用商品的人）；句意是每位消费者都有权获得清楚的信息。

senses.title: A buyer of goods
senses.definition: a person who buys products or services for personal use
senses.definitionCN: 为个人使用而购买产品或服务的人
senses.example: Consumers are demanding clearer labels.
senses.exampleCN: 消费者正在要求更清楚的标签。
senses.why: One receipt is small, but millions of receipts decide a market.
senses.whyCN: 一张小票不起眼，千百万张小票却能决定市场。

senses.title: A user of a service
senses.definition: a person who uses a service, especially media or utilities
